messages:
lina: Heads-up — trying to bring aurora-8k into the eval harness and seeing weird chat-template breaks around dataset entries that contain MIME-style headers (Content-Type / boundary lines).
lina: Short repro: tokenizer splits mid-header and the collate step then drops the sentinel, so chat fmt collapses.
matt: ugh, can you paste the raw snippet?
lina: ```
--boundary
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"role":"user","content":"Tell me a story"}
--boundary--
```
lina: After tokenization we end up with: `[...,'Content','-','Type',':','application','/','json', ...]` and later the chat-template collator expects the full header as a single token prefix so it trims it.
tasha: are these coming from the eval corpora or our scraped test fixtures?
lina: eval corpora — some multilingual samples include embedded email-like blocks. Not all models handle it consistently.
sam: sounds like a tokenizer normalization gap. aurora-8k uses a BPE variant that treats `-` and `/` differently. We should canonicalize MIME headers in the runner before tokenization.
matt: quick fix idea: preprocessor step that normalizes header lines to `Content-Type: application/json` (remove params), and replace boundaries with a single sentinel token `<<MIME_BOUNDARY>>`.
shane: +1. But watch the eval metric semantics — removing params might change prompt content for some tests (eg. charset differences). We need to flag which evals allow normalization.
lina: agreed. For now I put a throwaway branch that normalizes only for `eval/compatibility/*` suites. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/842
ci-bot: build 842 failed on linux-unit (runner-linter): token-splitter_test.py::test_mime_normalize flaked (timeout).
matt: flaky timeout in the test — looks like our collate waits on a join that gets stuck if the preprocessor emits sentinel tokens length > 1.
sam: I'm seeing the same locally: when sentinel is multi-token the prefix cache path doesn't match and a deadlock occurs in the continuous-batcher. I can reproduce with `pytest -k mime`.
shane: simplest safe change: make sentinel a single ascii char unlikely to appear (we used \u001f earlier but that caused logging issues). Propose `` (ETB) as internal marker and then map to readable `<<MIME_BOUNDARY>>` only in logs/dashboards.
tasha: If we use control char, need to ensure dashboards / ingestion (metrics pipeline) can handle it — otherwise telemetry will break. eval-bot: note — ingestion strips control chars in streaming consumer, so dashboards will show truncated prompts unless we map pre-ingest.
shane: ok then pipeline change: pre-ingest map control char -> `__MIME__` (safe ascii) for metric storage. I'll file a follow-up.
lina: TL;DR: landing PR 842 with a limited normalize-for-compatibility flag, switching sentinel to single-token control char, follow-up to map before telemetry.
matt: sounds good. can we add a small unit to assert that token count before/after normalization is within X% for load tests? want to catch regressions automatically.
sam: added to my local TODO. also adding a small eval diff test to CI to compare aurora-8k vs the float baseline on a 50-sample prompt set.
ci-bot: CI queued for PR 842: linux-unit, integration, eval-smoke.
eval-bot: FYI — when aurora-8k first reports, dashboard will create a new model entry; please annotate rollout in #eng-ml for alerting thresholds.
shane: I'll take the dashboard mapping task and add a small migration to the ingestion lambda to replace control char with `__MIME__`.
lina: thanks all — will update PR with sentinel change + tests. if CI is green I'll canary to dedicated staging tomorrow. :thumbsup:
